title: It's about to get a lot harder to keep countries honest about climate change | New Scientist
description: A row over when to publish crucial climate change assessments risks letting countries off the hook on emissions cuts
author: Madeleine Cuff

title: Bottlenose whales may look after each other when they’re sick | New Scientist
description: Northern bottlenose whales are more likely to stick together when individuals are poorly or emaciated
author: Jo Marchant

title: Discovery of T. rex's cousin upends our understanding of tyrannosaur evolution | New Scientist
description: A dinosaur that is new to science has features of both subfamilies of the tyrannosaur group, complicating our understanding of how they evolved
author: Jake Buehler

title: Error-correction record pushes quantum computers closer to usefulness | New Scientist
description: Useful quantum computers will have to use many “logical qubits” as their computational building blocks, and researchers just broke the record for how reliable they can be
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: El Niño is dramatically increasing sea levels – how bad could it get? | New Scientist
description: El Niño has already raised sea levels in part of the eastern Pacific by 40 centimetres and as it continues to strengthen, there could be coastal flooding from Alaska to Chile
author: Michael Le Page

title: Archaeologists are uncovering the meaning of a unique rock art site | New Scientist
description: Excavations in the Côa valley in Portugal, the world’s largest site of Palaeolithic open-air rock art, are yielding clues about how engravings of animals were seen by prehistoric hunter-gatherers
author: Benjamin Taub
